summary: r3 is a confirmation pass over the Architect's FINAL-cycle revision. My sole r2 line-item -- AT-2893 asserting 'exit 1' for UNSATISFIABLE against Sec 3.5/3.6's 'exit 3' -- is fixed: AT-2893 (line 295) now reads 'exit 3 (r3/fix-3: distinct from FAIL's exit 1, consistent with Sec 3.5/Sec 3.6 exit_code_for_fuzz)', and I grepped every remaining 'exit 1'/'UNSATISFIABLE' occurrence in the document (line-by-line) and found zero surviving contradictions -- Sec 3.5 (line 230), Sec 3.6 (line 237), Sec 10 (line 345), and the r3-changelog (line 386) all agree UNSATISFIABLE=exit 3 uniformly. I then verified the four r3 architectural deltas for internal coherence rather than re-litigating the pessimistic reviewer's r2 findings (already resolved by their own NEEDS_REVISION->this cycle): (1) the new UNCONSTRAINED_PRECONDITION_FIRED verdict is present in the Sec 3.5 verdict enum (line 190), correctly mapped SKIPPED-class/exit-0 in the Sec 3.6 exit table (line 237, 'PASS | SKIPPED | UNCONSTRAINED_PRECONDITION_FIRED -> 0'), and its reason.kind is documented (lines 216-217) -- no contradiction anywhere I could find. (2) The Sec 3.2(b) 4-quadrant table (lines 115-120) and the r3-changelog's restated table (lines 389-394) are byte-identical in content (same four rows, same reason.kind strings, same exit codes), and both correctly gate the quadrant classification on the CONSTRAINED subset only, with the deferred-condition exemption (Sec 3.2(b) lines 112, Sec 3.5 line 227) explicitly checked BEFORE the quadrant table is entered -- this is consistent with the oracle-triad section (Sec 3.2) where leg (b)'s discriminator is introduced: nothing in Sec 3.2(a)/(c) (legs a and c) references or conflicts with the quadrant machinery, which is scoped entirely to leg (b). (3) The all-f32 float pipeline (r3/C-1new) is stated consistently in Sec 3.4 (lines 161-169), Sec 3.5 (lines 219-220, 226), Sec 10's edge-case restatement (line 348), and the r3-changelog (line 384) -- same f32::MIN_POSITIVE FTZ-safe floor, same 'never f64' rule, same std430-decoded-bytes-actually-sent framing everywhere it appears; no lingering f64 reference survived outside of explicit 'NEVER f64' negations (confirmed by grep). (4) AT-2897's proven-firing pin procedure (r3/fix-5, lines 302, 397) correctly replaces the r2 probabilistic approach with a Coder-measured-once, seed-pinned deterministic assertion, closing the pessimistic reviewer's W-1new seed-flakiness concern without touching the sampler's underlying formula.
strengths: AT-2893 fix confirmed exact and complete: 'exit 3 (r3/fix-3: ...)' at line 295, cross-referenced against Sec 3.5 (line 230, 'Exit 3'), Sec 3.6 (line 237, 'UNSATISFIABLE -> 3'), and Sec 10 (line 345, 'AT-2893, exit 3') -- all four sites now agree; this was my only r2 concern and it is resolved verbatim as I suggested.

The new UNCONSTRAINED_PRECONDITION_FIRED verdict class is threaded through every touchpoint I checked -- Sec 3.2(b) introduction (lines 112, with the exit-0/SKIPPED-class justification spelled out), Sec 3.5 verdict enum + prose (lines 190, 216-217, 232), Sec 3.6 exit-code table (line 237), Sec 10 edge case (line 346), and AT-2892's new unit (line 294) -- with no contradicting exit code or verdict-string variant found anywhere.

The 4-quadrant table appears twice (Sec 3.2(b) lines 115-120, r3-changelog lines 389-394) and is verbatim-identical in both places -- same reason.kind strings (precondition_check_miscompiled / satisfier_unsound / satisfier_unsound_or_check_inert), same exit codes (1/2/2), same host-vs-GPU axis definitions -- eliminating the risk of a Coder finding two subtly different specs to implement against.

The 4-quadrant table is correctly scoped as leg-(b)-internal machinery: the oracle triad's legs (a) device-fault and (c) determinism (Sec 3.2, unchanged from r2) make no reference to the discriminator and are not affected by its totality upgrade -- the quadrant table augments only the postcondition-oracle leg's precondition-bit discriminator, exactly where it was introduced in r1/r2.

The all-f32 rule (r3/C-1new) closes the pessimistic reviewer's CRITICAL C-1new cleanly: f32::MIN_POSITIVE is explicitly chosen (not the smallest subnormal) specifically because it is FTZ-safe, directly answering the vendor_concerns note in the r2 pessimistic review about NVIDIA/AMD flush-to-zero divergence from Lavapipe -- confirmed at line 166 and restated at line 384.

AT-2897's pin procedure (r3/fix-5) is a sound resolution of seed-flakiness: rather than asserting a formula guarantees a >=1000 draw (which r2's pessimistic review proved false for a lower-bounded-only window), it requires the Coder to measure once, confirm firing, and pin the exact (seed, window, runs) triple as AT constants -- this is the standard fix for RNG-stream-dependent test determinism and includes an explicit re-pin maintenance note for toolchain RNG changes.

LOC table (Sec 12, line 371) shows the discriminator helper grew from ~30 to ~55 LOC (r2->r3) for the f32 re-check + totality + exemption logic, consistent with the r3-changelog's stated total nudge '~1330 -> ~1355' (line 399); cap ~1700 unchanged and still comfortably absorbs it.
external_references: IEEE 754-2008 Sec 5.3.1 (nextUp/nextDown) -- r3's f32-only nextafter fix (f32::next_up()/next_down(), or an explicit bit-increment fallback) is the textbook single-precision analogue of the r2 fix, now correctly scoped to the precision the DSL actually uses (F32 is the only DebugCheck float type per ty.rs:23/hir.rs:157, as independently confirmed by the pessimistic reviewer's own code citations).

GPU flush-to-zero (FTZ) denormal handling (common NVIDIA/AMD compute-pipeline behavior for f32) -- f32::MIN_POSITIVE (smallest NORMAL f32, ~1.18e-38) surviving FTZ where the smallest SUBNORMAL (~1.4e-45) would not is a well-known GPU numerics caveat; r3's choice is the standard cross-vendor-safe answer.

Design by Contract (Bertrand Meyer, 1992) -- the precondition/postcondition oracle triad, now with a total (all-quadrants-defined) discriminator, remains a faithful and now more complete instance of contract verification: totality is precisely what makes the discriminator a sound classifier rather than a partial one that silently drops a failure mode.
summary_verdict: APPROVE (r3, FINAL cycle).
